diagnosis.narrative: The series is dominated by a strong upward trend (a net rise of ~13% of its level). Seasonality is strong (period 52): a repeating cycle explains much of the movement. The spectrum is close to white noise, so most of the variation is irregular and hard to predict. The series reads as ambiguous by the ADF/KPSS tests. A few outliers stand out (1 points, ~1% of the sample). Across validation windows the model ranking is unstable (Kendall tau -0.107), which favours a robust combination.

We haven't tested E, F, G, H. Let's pick a different kind: maybe median pool4. That uses different combine. So test G.

attempts.rationale: The series has high trend and seasonality but ranking is unstable; a simple mean over all models may provide robust performance.
Try a weighted combination using softmax_neg_error to see if a more nuanced weighting improves over the simple mean, given the unstable ranking and high correlation groups.
The series has very high trend and seasonality but ranking is unstable; a robust central tendency like median may help reduce influence of outlier models.
Try a per‑horizon weighted mean using the top‑k mean per horizon handle (w3) to see if horizon‑specific averaging improves robustness in this mixed, low‑predictability series.
test a trimmed mean to see if removing extreme high‑error models improves robustness given unstable ranking and high outliers.
Use a simple inverse‑error weighting to see if a data‑driven weight improves over the current softmax hint, given the unstable ranking and high outliers.
The series has high trend/seasonality but unstable ranking and many correlated errors; a robust DBA may exploit complementary models.
test a per‑horizon weighted combination using inverse_error (w5) to see if horizon‑specific weights improve over the overall weighted mean, given unstable ranking and high outliers.
use top-7 models with softmax weights to leverage complementary models
Use a per‑horizon best‑model weighting to capture the strong seasonal trend and the unstable ranking across windows.
focus on top 7 models with inverse-error weighting
The series has unstable ranking and many correlated errors; a robust median over a correlated cluster pool may help reduce variance.

decision.justification: Selected 'weighted weighted by w2' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.9936. Series context: trend strength 0.9994 and seasonal strength 0.9999; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau -0.107); 6 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.644.
